accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE (2013) English programmes of study, Year 1 word reading (apply phonic knowledge to decode words; respond speedily with the correct sound to graphemes for all 40+ phonemes; read accurately by blending sounds in unfamiliar words containing taught GPCs), the DfE Reading Framework (2023) description of blending and sound buttons, and Common Core RF.K.3, RF.1.2b (blend sounds including consonant blends), RF.1.3a (common consonant digraphs) and RF.1.3b. Every lab word is phonically regular: sh, ch and ck are each one phoneme, c and ck both say k, and frog, stop and crab each have four phonemes with an adjacent-consonant onset. Vowel sounds are short (a as in apple), and the long-vowel letter names appear only as wrong options.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early-reading errors: adding a schwa to each phoneme (suh, puh, tuh as wrong cards in Pure sounds, uh tag, p3), letter names in place of sounds (you, eye, ay cards, name tag), saying the sounds without merging them (the m-a-p prediction, m5), splitting digraphs (s-h-i-p prediction, split tag, m2), dropping one of two adjacent consonants (Just f: f-o-g prediction, fog for frog, drop tag, m4), reading right to left (dragging the car backwards gives 'Blend from left to right', order tag, nus in m1) and guessing from the first letter (big/bag/bog, pan/pen/pin, dig/dog/dug in Read every sound, m3).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagblend is built on the act of blending itself: grapheme tiles with sound buttons (dots for single letters, a dash for a digraph), a car driven along the blending arrow that lights each sound as it passes and then slides the sound bubbles together into the word, and letter tiles that fuse into a digraph tile when tapped. Shingle similarity is 8.2% with flag_sorry.js, 7.8% with flag_poss.js and lower with every other lab, including flag_phon.js (single letter sounds) and the onset-rime lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers each rule by doing: the word only appears after the car reaches the end of the arrow, so sounds alone are not reading; a tile marked with a dash shows sh is one sound before the text says 'count sounds, not letters'; wrong word cards name the exact sound that differs ('Check the middle sound: a, not i'); and the four-sound words light four buttons, so a skipped consonant is visible. Done lines then confirm the rule and quote the child's prediction.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the next task disproves: 'Yes, I said the sounds' (the word only comes after the push together), '4, one for each letter' for ship (the s and h fuse into one tile and one dash), and 'Just f: f-o-g' for frog (the car lights four sound buttons, f and r both). A.reveal quotes the child's own pick in each done message.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions with tagged wrong answers; why() names the specific slip for each: order ('Blend from left to right. The first sound comes first'), vowel ('Check the middle sound too'), split ('Two letters can make one sound: sh, ch, th, ck'), drop ('When two consonants sit together, say both'), uh ('Muh-a-tuh is hard to blend. Say mmm') and name ('Em is the letter name'). Every wrong move inside the lab also explains itself (UHWHY per letter, digraph and word-card messages).

readability.evidence: Kid text measures FK -0.4 in very short concrete sentences ('m, a, p. Map!'), against the family kid limit. Adult text measures FK 9.0 (limit 9.5) and uses the precise terms phoneme, grapheme, GPC, digraph, sound buttons, CVC, CCVC and adjacent consonants (consonant blend), with the Year 1 and RF.K.3, RF.1.2b, RF.1.3b standard references.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate passed; the largest 6-word-shingle overlap with any other lesson is 1.0% (Single Letter Sounds). Kid paragraphs cover blending left to right, pure sounds, digraph teams and reading every sound; adult paragraphs give the curriculum placement, the key terms, five named mistakes with a fix, and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark for every step: grapheme tiles (about 64 px) with sound buttons fit the width for the 5-letter chick and the 4-letter frog, the car and arrow sit under the buttons, the picture and blended word show below, the sss/suh cards and the three word cards fit one row, and young-mode buttons below are at least 56 px tall.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: all five Show me tasks completed, the challenge appeared, axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in either theme and there were no console errors. A manual probe dragged the car (map blended), tapped letters (i rejected with a reason, s joined sh), dragged bag onto the picture and picked suh then sss. Every drag has a button twin (Drive, each letter, each word, each sound card) and the canvas aria-label is updated with every message.
